title: Theorem 8.9.6
section: 8.9 Bounded potentials and recursive Hessian currents
text: Theorem 8.9.6 . 846671D5582A For $1\leq p\leq m$, $Q_ p$ is a positive current of order zero, and \[  \int _ KQ_ p\wedge \omega ^{m-p} \leq C_{K,U,\omega ,p}(1+M)^ p.  \] It is the iterated limit, in the order of ( 8.9.4 ), of \[  (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1^{j_1})\wedge \cdots \wedge (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ p^{j_ p})\wedge \omega ^{n-m}.  \] In particular $Q_ m$ is a positive Radon measure. These currents are local in the canonical potentials and independent of the chosen approximations for the fixed ordering. When all potentials are continuous, $Q_ p$ equals the continuous mixed product of 8.7.1 . Proof. Expand the smooth shifted product over its subsets. Applying ( 8.9.4 ) to each subset, in its inherited ordering, gives ( 8.9.5 ). The absent indices have no effect on a subset's limit. Each smooth product is positive: pairing with a decomposable strongly positive complementary test appends $m-p$ nonnegative rank-one $(1,1)$-forms, and polarized Gårding positivity applies. The smooth mixed mass bound is uniform in all indices. Distributional limits preserve positivity and the local trace bound at every step. Positive currents have order zero, so this gives the assertions for $Q_ p$, including the top-degree measure. The recursion uses only bounded multiplication of canonical values and local distributional differentiation. It is therefore local. Its definition contains no approximation choices, so the proved limit is independent of those choices while the ordering is fixed. For continuous potentials, the approximations converge uniformly by Dini's theorem. The telescoping estimate in 8.7.1 is uniform in all remaining indices and shows that their iterated limit is the same continuous mixed product. This also proves permutation invariance in the continuous case. $\square$

title: Proposition 8.9.7
section: 8.9 Bounded potentials and recursive Hessian currents
text: Proposition 8.9.7 . 26EFAEC0B76D Write $R_{p-1}^{\widehat a}$ for the shifted current obtained by omitting $u_ a$, in the inherited order, and use two hats for two omissions. Put $R_0=1$. For $1\leq p\leq m$, \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm dR_ p& =\mathrm d\omega \wedge \sum _{a=1}^ pR_{p-1}^{\widehat a},\\  \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}R_ p& =\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \sum _{a=1}^ pR_{p-1}^{\widehat a},\\  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}R_ p& =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega \wedge \sum _{a=1}^ pR_{p-1}^{\widehat a} +2\, \mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \sum _{a<b}R_{p-2}^{\widehat a\widehat b}. \end{aligned}  \] The last sum is absent for $p=1$. All currents on the right have order zero. If all but at most one potential are smooth, $R_ p$ is independent of the ordering and is the ordinary product of the smooth factors with $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$. Proof. Every $D_ I$ is both $\mathrm d$- and $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$-closed. Differentiating ( 8.9.5 ) therefore gives \[  \mathrm dR_ p=\mathrm d\omega \wedge \sum _ I(p-|I|)\omega ^{p-|I|-1}\wedge D_ I,  \] with zero terms omitted. The coefficient $p-|I|$ counts the omitted indices outside $I$, which proves the first formula; the second is identical with $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ in place of $\mathrm d$. Apply $\mathrm d$ to the second formula. Each pair of omitted indices occurs twice, and $-\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \mathrm d\omega =\mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ because both forms have odd degree three. This gives the displayed $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ formula, with every background derivative retained. If all but one potential are smooth, applying $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ to the bounded potential times a smooth closed product gives its $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ wedged with that product. At later smooth steps, closedness again makes the recursion ordinary smooth multiplication. This is independent of the position of the bounded potential, and the subset expansion gives the last assertion. $\square$

title: Lemma 8.9.8
section: 8.9 Bounded potentials and recursive Hessian currents
text: Lemma 8.9.8 . A1E60FC7AA88 Let $U$ be a coordinate ball compactly contained in a holomorphic chart. There is a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic $\rho $ on a neighborhood of $\overline U$ such that $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho \geq 2\omega $ and, for every bounded admissible $u$ on $X$, $u+\rho $ is $m$-subharmonic relative to $\omega $ on $U$. Adding $\rho $ to the approximations in 8.6.6 gives uniformly bounded smooth decreasing approximations in this local class. Proof. Take $\rho =C|z|^2$ in the chart. On the fixed compact set $\overline U$, a sufficiently large $C$ gives $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho \geq 2\omega $. An upper test $q$ for $u+\rho $ at $x$ gives the upper test $q-\rho $ for $u$ there. Hence \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q=(\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(q-\rho ))+(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho -\omega ) \in \overline{\Gamma _ m(\omega )},  \] since the second summand is positive and the cone is preserved by adding nonnegative forms. Smooth addition preserves the canonical representative. The same identity applies pointwise to every smooth admissible approximation. Adding a fixed smooth function preserves pointwise decrease and convergence, and its bounded norm on $\overline U$ preserves the common local bound. $\square$

title: Example 8.9.9
section: 8.9 Bounded potentials and recursive Hessian currents
text: Example 8.9.9 . 5F56B4D9CC35 On the unit ball in $\mathbb C^3$, put $\beta _ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z_ j|^2$, $\beta =\sum _{j=1}^3\beta _ j$ and \[  u=-\tfrac 12\sum _{j=1}^3|z_ j|^2, \qquad v=-\tfrac 45|z_1|^2.  \] Both $\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ and $\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$ are strictly positive, but \[  (\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^2\wedge \beta > (\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2\wedge \beta , \qquad (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^2\wedge \beta <(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^2\wedge \beta .  \] Thus shifted Hessian order does not imply unshifted Hessian order, even for smooth potentials with positive perturbed forms. Proof. The eigenvalues of the two perturbed forms relative to $\beta $ are $(\tfrac 12,\tfrac 12,\tfrac 12)$ and $(\tfrac 15,1,1)$. For a diagonal form with relative eigenvalues $\lambda _1,\lambda _2, \lambda _3$, its second Hessian is $(\lambda _1\lambda _2+\lambda _1\lambda _3+\lambda _2\lambda _3)\beta ^3/3$. Consequently the shifted measures of $u,v$ are $\tfrac 14\beta ^3$ and $\tfrac 7{15}\beta ^3$, while their unshifted expressions are $\tfrac 14\beta ^3$ and $0$. Their unshifted traces are negative, so neither original function belongs to the local unshifted class. Adding $\sum _ j|z_ j|^2$ gives an exact correction in this constant closed background. An exact correction $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho =\omega $ is impossible where $\mathrm d\omega \ne 0$. $\square$

title: 8.10 Sobolev capacity and two Hessian factors
search_title: Sobolev capacity and two Hessian factors
section: 8.10 Sobolev capacity and two Hessian factors
text:
To multiply a varying coefficient measure by a bounded potential, weak convergence of the measures is not enough. We first control the sets on which a potential can be discontinuous. The linear trace of an admissible form supplies this control through Sobolev capacity. Its Gauduchon multiplier must be chosen in the conformal class of $\omega $, since an admissible form need not be positive in every tangent direction. Choose $ho >0$ by theorem 11.4.2 and put \[  T=ho \omega ^{n-1},\qquad \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T=0,\qquad A=\int _ X\omega \wedge T>0.  \] Write $H^1(X)=W^{1,2}(X,\mathbb R)$ and use the equivalent Sobolev norm \[  \| f\| _{H^1}^2=\int _ Xf^2\omega ^ n+ \int _ X\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge T.  \] For an open set $G\subset X$ define \[  \operatorname {Cap}_1(G) =\inf \{ \| f\| _{H^1}^2:f\in H^1(X),\  f\geq 1 	ext{ almost everywhere on }G\} ,  \] and for an arbitrary set $E$ take the infimum over open $G\supset E$. Thus this capacity is defined by Sobolev energy; it is distinct from an $m$-Hessian capacity. Truncation allows $0\leq f\leq 1$ in the infimum for open sets. Lemma 8.10.1 . EB20E121128A The capacity $\operatorname {Cap}_1$ is countably subadditive. For a smooth real $f$ and $a>0$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_1(\{ |f|>a\} )\leq a^{-2}\| f\| _{H^1}^2.  \] If a positive Radon measure $\mu $ satisfies $|\int _ X\phi \, \mathrm d\mu |\leq C\| \phi \| _{H^1}$ for every smooth real $\phi $, then for every Borel set $E$, \[  \mu (E)\leq C\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)^{1/2}.  \] Proof. For open $G_ i$ choose Sobolev functions $0\leq f_ i\leq 1$ equal to one almost everywhere on $G_ i$, with a summably small excess in their squared norms over the capacity infima. The Sobolev chain rule gives \[  \| \max _{i\leq N}f_ i\| _{H^1}^2\leq \sum _{i\leq N}\| f_ i\| _{H^1}^2.  \] Indeed, almost everywhere the gradient of the maximum is the gradient of an active function, and the squared value is bounded by the sum of the squared values. If the sum is finite, these maxima converge in $L^2$, are bounded in $H^1$, and have a weak $H^1$ limit equal to one almost everywhere on $ igcup _ iG_ i$. Lower semicontinuity proves subadditivity for open sets. Taking open supersets proves it for arbitrary sets. If the sum is infinite there is nothing to prove. The level-set estimate follows by testing with $\min \{ 1,|f|/a\} $ and the same Sobolev chain rule. Fix a compact $K\subset G$ and a Sobolev competitor $0\leq f\leq 1$ for the open set $G$. Positive local mollification and a partition of unity give smooth nonnegative $f_\epsilon 	o f$ in $H^1$ that satisfy $f_\epsilon \geq 1$ on $K$ for small $\epsilon $: every convolution ball meeting $K$ then lies in $G$, where $f=1$ almost everywhere. The assumed estimate gives $\mu (K)\leq C\lim _\epsilon \| f_\epsilon \| _{H^1}=C\| f\| _{H^1}$. Take the infimum over $f$ and then the supremum over compact $K\subset G$ to obtain the estimate for $G$. Outer regularity and open supersets give it for every Borel $E$. $\square$ Lemma 8.10.2 . FFBF9CD42640 Every bounded admissible $u$ belongs to $H^1(X)$. Its trace \[  \mu _ u=(\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)\wedge T  \] is a positive Radon measure of total mass $A$. If $\| u\| _\infty \leq M$, then \[  \| u\| _{H^1}\leq C(1+M),\qquad \mu _ u(E)\leq C(1+M)\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)^{1/2}  \] for every Borel $E$. On each fixed relatively compact coordinate chart, the total variation of every coefficient of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ is also bounded on $E$ by $C(1+M)\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)^{1/2}$. Proof. First let $u$ be smooth admissible. The first-cone inequality gives $\mu _ u\geq 0$, since $T$ is conformal to $\omega ^{n-1}$, and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T=0$ gives $\mu _ u(X)=A$. Applying distributional Stokes to $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u^2)$ yields the energy identity \[  \int _ X\mathrm du\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}u\wedge T =-\int _ Xu\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge T =-\int _ Xu\, \mathrm d\mu _ u+\int _ Xu\omega \wedge T \leq 2MA.  \] Together with the $L^2$ bound this controls $\| u\| _{H^1}$. For bounded admissible $u$, choose smooth admissible $u_ j\downarrow u$ by 8.6.6 , discard a finite initial segment, and take $\| u_ j\| _\infty \leq M+1$ as in 8.9.1 . Bounded convergence gives strong $L^2$ convergence. The energy bound gives weak $H^1$ compactness, and every weak cluster point agrees with $u$ in $L^2$; thus the entire sequence converges weakly to $u$ in $H^1$. This proves the Sobolev bound. The trace measures converge weakly to $\mu _ u$, preserving positivity and total mass. For any smooth real $\phi $, the first-order Stokes identity is \[  \int _ X\phi \, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge T =-\int _ X\mathrm d\phi \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}u\wedge T +\int _ X\phi \, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}u\wedge \mathrm dT.  \] It remains valid for $u\in H^1$ by smooth Sobolev approximation. Both terms are bounded by $C\| u\| _{H^1}\| \phi \| _{H^1}$; the background term $\int \phi \omega \wedge T$ is bounded by $C\| \phi \| _{H^1}$. The preceding capacity lemma gives the bound for $\mu _ u$. In particular the derivative $\mathrm dT$ has not been discarded. For a smooth admissible approximant, write the eigenvalues of $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$ in an $\omega $-unitary frame as $\lambda _ i$. Since $m\geq 2$, \[  \sum _ i\lambda _ i^2\leq \left(\sum _ i\lambda _ iight)^2, \qquad \sum _ i\lambda _ i\geq 0.  \] Consequently every coefficient of this form is dominated by its trace. On a fixed coordinate chart this bounds the coefficient variations of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$ by $C(\mu _{u_ j}+\omega ^ n)$. Passing to the weak measure limits of 8.9.1 gives the same domination by $C(\mu _ u+\omega ^ n)$. Finally $\int _ E\omega ^ n\leq \operatorname {Cap}_1(E)$ and $\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)\leq \| 1\| _{H^1}^2$ absorb the smooth term into the claimed square-root estimate. $\square$ Lemma 8.10.3 . A82044827575 Every bounded canonical admissible potential is continuous on the complement of an open set of arbitrarily small $\operatorname {Cap}_1$. The same open set can be chosen for any countable family of such potentials. Proof. Choose smooth admissible $u_ j\downarrow u$. By the preceding lemma these functions converge weakly to $u$ in $H^1$. Mazur's lemma gives finite convex combinations $w_ N$ of terms with $j\geq N$ such that \[  \| w_ N-u\| _{H^1}\leq 8^{-N}.  \] Because $u\leq w_ N\leq u_ N$, they converge pointwise to the canonical function $u$, not just to an unspecified almost-everywhere representative. Put \[  G_{N_0}= igcup _{N\geq N_0} \{ |w_{N+1}-w_ N|>2^{-N}\} .  \] The capacity tools imply \[  \operatorname {Cap}_1(G_{N_0}) \leq \sum _{N\geq N_0}4^ N\| w_{N+1}-w_ N\| _{H^1}^2 \leq C\sum _{N\geq N_0}16^{-N}\longrightarrow 0.  \] Outside $G_{N_0}$, the successive differences form a uniformly summable series. Thus $w_ N$ converge uniformly there and their limit $u$ is continuous on that closed set. For a countable family, choose the exceptional open sets with capacities less than $\epsilon 2^{-i}$ and take their union. Countable subadditivity proves the last assertion. $\square$ Proposition 8.10.4 . B40742E0DD08 Suppose $u_ j\downarrow u$ and $v_ j\downarrow v$ are bounded canonical admissible potentials with a common uniform bound. Then \[  v_ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j\longrightarrow v\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u  \] weakly as currents with signed measure coefficients. The same conclusion holds for $v_ j\mu _{u_ j}	o v\mu _ u$. Proof. Bounded convergence gives $u_ j	o u$ in $L^1$. Their complex Hessians therefore converge in distributions. The preceding coefficient bounds are uniform, so this is weak convergence of each signed coefficient measure against continuous compactly supported tests. The trace measures also converge weakly. Every one of these measures has total variation bounded by $C_ M\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)^{1/2}$ on a Borel set $E$. Fix $\epsilon >0$. Quasicontinuity supplies an open $G$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_1(G)<\epsilon $ on whose complement $v$ and every $v_ j$ are continuous. Dini's theorem on the compact set $X\setminus G$ gives uniform convergence there. Extend $v|_{X\setminus G}$ to a continuous function $F$ on $X$ with the same uniform bound, by Tietze's theorem. For any one of the signed coefficient measures $
u _ j	o 
u $ and a fixed continuous compactly supported test $\psi $, subtract $F
u _ j$ and $F
u $. The resulting error is at most \[  C_{M,\psi } igl (\| v_ j-v\| _{X\setminus G} +\epsilon ^{1/2} igr ).  \] The term with $F$ converges by weak measure convergence. First let $j	o \infty $ and then $\epsilon \downarrow 0$. This proves the assertion for the Hessian coefficients and for the positive trace measures. $\square$ Theorem 8.10.5 . 0241EC758621 For two bounded admissible potentials $u,v$, the recursive current $D_2(u,v)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)$ is symmetric in its arguments. If $u_ j\downarrow u$ and $v_ j\downarrow v$ are bounded admissible sequences with a common uniform bound, then \[  D_2(u_ j,v_ j)\longrightarrow D_2(u,v)  \] in distributions. Their shifted positive currents \[  Q_2(u,v)= igl (\omega ^2+\omega \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u +\omega \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v+D_2(u,v) igr )\wedge \omega ^{n-m}  \] converge weakly as positive currents. For $m=2$ these are positive Radon measures. For $m>2$, the unwedged $D_2$ also converges weakly as a current with measure coefficients. Proof. For smooth admissible approximations $u_ k\downarrow u$ and $v_ k\downarrow v$, the weighted convergence proposition gives \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ k\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k)\longrightarrow \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u).  \] The smooth current on the left is $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ k\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k$ and is symmetric. Applying the same argument in the opposite order proves $D_2(u,v)=D_2(v,u)$. For the bounded sequences in the statement, weighted convergence followed by $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ gives the asserted simultaneous distributional limit. The displayed subset expansion is the current of 8.9.6 with $p=2$. Its lower-degree terms converge weakly, so its whole distributional limit is $Q_2(u,v)$. Positivity and the uniform local mass bounds turn this into weak convergence of currents of order zero. When $m>2$, the same conclusion for $D_2$ follows from the uniform coefficient bounds below degree $m$ in 8.9.3 . $\square$ The capacity estimate depends on using a first Hessian. A product of two Hessians can already charge a set of zero Sobolev capacity. Lemma 8.10.6 . 2A6BE9847309 Let $E$ be a compact subset of a smooth real submanifold of codimension two contained in a coordinate chart. Then $\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)=0$. Proof. It suffices to treat a compact subset of a submanifold chart, since finitely many such subsets cover $E$ and the capacity is subadditive. Choose real coordinates $(s,t)$ there, with $t\in \mathbb R^2$ and the submanifold given by $t=0$. Choose $0\leq \eta \leq 1$ smooth, supported in this chart and equal to one near the compact subset. Put $r=|t|$. For $0<\epsilon <1/2$ define \[  h_\epsilon (r)=  egin{cases}  1,& 0\leq r\leq \epsilon ^2,\  \displaystyle  rac{\log (\epsilon /r)}{\log (1/\epsilon )}, & \epsilon ^2<r<\epsilon ,\  0,& r\geq \epsilon . \end{cases}  \] The Sobolev function $f_\epsilon =\eta h_\epsilon $ equals one on an open neighborhood of that subset. On the fixed compact coordinate set the Sobolev norm is equivalent to the Euclidean one. Integration in the two normal variables gives \[  \| f_\epsilon \| _{H^1}^2 \leq C\left(\epsilon ^2+ \int _{\epsilon ^2}^{\epsilon }  rac{\mathrm dr}{r\log (1/\epsilon )^2}ight) =C\left(\epsilon ^2+ rac1{\log (1/\epsilon )}ight) \longrightarrow 0.  \] The derivatives of $\eta $ contribute at most $C\epsilon ^2$. Taking the infimum over open neighborhoods proves the assertion. $\square$ Example 8.10.7 . AEB4F2397BBF There are bounded continuous $\omega $-plurisubharmonic potentials $u,v$ and a compact Borel set $E$ such that \[  \operatorname {Cap}_1(E)=0,\qquad \int _ E Q_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{m-2}>0.  \] Consequently the first-Hessian capacity estimate does not extend to this positive two-factor measure, even within the continuous $\omega $-plurisubharmonic subclass. Proof. Choose holomorphic coordinates $z_ j=x_ j+\mathrm i y_ j$ and a smooth nonnegative cutoff $\chi $ supported in the chart and equal to one on a smaller coordinate box. Extend \[  u=a\chi |x_1|,\qquad v=a\chi |x_2|  \] by zero outside the chart. These functions are globally continuous and bounded. To check their curvature, replace $|x_ j|$ by $g_\delta (x_ j)=(x_ j^2+\delta ^2)^{1/2}$, with $0<\delta \leq 1$. The Hessian of $\chi g_\delta $ has the nonnegative term $\chi \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_\delta $; all its remaining terms are uniformly bounded forms, since $g_\delta $ and $g_\delta '$ are uniformly bounded on the fixed support. Thus $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi g_\delta )\geq -C\omega $ with $C$ independent of $\delta $. Choosing $a>0$ sufficiently small gives $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(a\chi g_\delta )\geq \omega /2$ for both coordinates. Their decreasing limits $u,v$ are therefore $\omega $-plurisubharmonic and admissible. On the box where $\chi =1$, set $\alpha _ j= rac{\mathrm i}{4\pi }\mathrm dz_ j\wedge \mathrm d ar z_ j$. The book's normalization gives \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_\delta (x_ j)=	frac 12g_\delta ''(x_ j)\alpha _ j, \qquad g_\delta ''(x_ j) = rac{\delta ^2}{(x_ j^2+\delta ^2)^{3/2}} \longrightarrow 2\delta _{\{ x_ j=0\} }.  \] The measures $g_\delta ^{\prime \prime }(t)\, \mathrm dt$ have mass two, while their mass outside any fixed neighborhood of zero tends to zero. The two smooth factors depend on distinct real variables, so their product is an approximate identity in $(x_1,x_2)$ and converges to the tensor-product measure. By 8.10.5 , locally \[  D_2(u,v)=a^2\delta _{\{ x_1=0\} }\delta _{\{ x_2=0\} } \alpha _1\wedge \alpha _2.  \] Choose $E$ to be a compact piece of $\{ x_1=x_2=0\} $ inside this box with nonempty relative interior. The preceding lemma gives $\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)=0$. On this box, the positive measure $D_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{n-2}$ has strictly positive mass on $E$, since $\omega $ is strictly positive. The smooth term $\omega ^ n$ and the two single-Hessian terms in the expansion \[  Q_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{m-2} =\omega ^ n+\omega ^{n-1}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v) +D_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{n-2}  \] have zero mass on $E$: each single-Hessian term is absolutely continuous in the other normal real variable. Hence the asserted mass is strictly positive. A bound by $C\operatorname {Cap}_1(F)^ b$ for all Borel $F$, with any $b>0$, would contradict this choice of $E$. $\square$ The preceding Sobolev-capacity estimate therefore cannot be iterated to control higher-degree coefficient measures. A local Hessian capacity supplies that control in the next section.

title: Lemma 8.10.1
section: 8.10 Sobolev capacity and two Hessian factors
text: Lemma 8.10.1 . EB20E121128A The capacity $\operatorname {Cap}_1$ is countably subadditive. For a smooth real $f$ and $a>0$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_1(\{ |f|>a\} )\leq a^{-2}\| f\| _{H^1}^2.  \] If a positive Radon measure $\mu $ satisfies $|\int _ X\phi \, \mathrm d\mu |\leq C\| \phi \| _{H^1}$ for every smooth real $\phi $, then for every Borel set $E$, \[  \mu (E)\leq C\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)^{1/2}.  \] Proof. For open $G_ i$ choose Sobolev functions $0\leq f_ i\leq 1$ equal to one almost everywhere on $G_ i$, with a summably small excess in their squared norms over the capacity infima. The Sobolev chain rule gives \[  \| \max _{i\leq N}f_ i\| _{H^1}^2\leq \sum _{i\leq N}\| f_ i\| _{H^1}^2.  \] Indeed, almost everywhere the gradient of the maximum is the gradient of an active function, and the squared value is bounded by the sum of the squared values. If the sum is finite, these maxima converge in $L^2$, are bounded in $H^1$, and have a weak $H^1$ limit equal to one almost everywhere on $\bigcup _ iG_ i$. Lower semicontinuity proves subadditivity for open sets. Taking open supersets proves it for arbitrary sets. If the sum is infinite there is nothing to prove. The level-set estimate follows by testing with $\min \{ 1,|f|/a\} $ and the same Sobolev chain rule. Fix a compact $K\subset G$ and a Sobolev competitor $0\leq f\leq 1$ for the open set $G$. Positive local mollification and a partition of unity give smooth nonnegative $f_\epsilon \to f$ in $H^1$ that satisfy $f_\epsilon \geq 1$ on $K$ for small $\epsilon $: every convolution ball meeting $K$ then lies in $G$, where $f=1$ almost everywhere. The assumed estimate gives $\mu (K)\leq C\lim _\epsilon \| f_\epsilon \| _{H^1}=C\| f\| _{H^1}$. Take the infimum over $f$ and then the supremum over compact $K\subset G$ to obtain the estimate for $G$. Outer regularity and open supersets give it for every Borel $E$. $\square$

title: Lemma 8.10.2
section: 8.10 Sobolev capacity and two Hessian factors
text: Lemma 8.10.2 . FFBF9CD42640 Every bounded admissible $u$ belongs to $H^1(X)$. Its trace \[  \mu _ u=(\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)\wedge T  \] is a positive Radon measure of total mass $A$. If $\| u\| _\infty \leq M$, then \[  \| u\| _{H^1}\leq C(1+M),\qquad \mu _ u(E)\leq C(1+M)\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)^{1/2}  \] for every Borel $E$. On each fixed relatively compact coordinate chart, the total variation of every coefficient of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ is also bounded on $E$ by $C(1+M)\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)^{1/2}$. Proof. First let $u$ be smooth admissible. The first-cone inequality gives $\mu _ u\geq 0$, since $T$ is conformal to $\omega ^{n-1}$, and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T=0$ gives $\mu _ u(X)=A$. Applying distributional Stokes to $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u^2)$ yields the energy identity \[  \int _ X\mathrm du\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}u\wedge T =-\int _ Xu\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge T =-\int _ Xu\, \mathrm d\mu _ u+\int _ Xu\omega \wedge T \leq 2MA.  \] Together with the $L^2$ bound this controls $\| u\| _{H^1}$. For bounded admissible $u$, choose smooth admissible $u_ j\downarrow u$ by 8.6.6 , discard a finite initial segment, and take $\| u_ j\| _\infty \leq M+1$ as in 8.9.1 . Bounded convergence gives strong $L^2$ convergence. The energy bound gives weak $H^1$ compactness, and every weak cluster point agrees with $u$ in $L^2$; thus the entire sequence converges weakly to $u$ in $H^1$. This proves the Sobolev bound. The trace measures converge weakly to $\mu _ u$, preserving positivity and total mass. For any smooth real $\phi $, the first-order Stokes identity is \[  \int _ X\phi \, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge T =-\int _ X\mathrm d\phi \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}u\wedge T +\int _ X\phi \, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}u\wedge \mathrm dT.  \] It remains valid for $u\in H^1$ by smooth Sobolev approximation. Both terms are bounded by $C\| u\| _{H^1}\| \phi \| _{H^1}$; the background term $\int \phi \omega \wedge T$ is bounded by $C\| \phi \| _{H^1}$. The preceding capacity lemma gives the bound for $\mu _ u$. In particular the derivative $\mathrm dT$ has not been discarded. For a smooth admissible approximant, write the eigenvalues of $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$ in an $\omega $-unitary frame as $\lambda _ i$. Since $m\geq 2$, \[  \sum _ i\lambda _ i^2\leq \left(\sum _ i\lambda _ i\right)^2, \qquad \sum _ i\lambda _ i\geq 0.  \] Consequently every coefficient of this form is dominated by its trace. On a fixed coordinate chart this bounds the coefficient variations of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j$ by $C(\mu _{u_ j}+\omega ^ n)$. Passing to the weak measure limits of 8.9.1 gives the same domination by $C(\mu _ u+\omega ^ n)$. Finally $\int _ E\omega ^ n\leq \operatorname {Cap}_1(E)$ and $\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)\leq \| 1\| _{H^1}^2$ absorb the smooth term into the claimed square-root estimate. $\square$

title: Lemma 8.10.3
section: 8.10 Sobolev capacity and two Hessian factors
text: Lemma 8.10.3 . A82044827575 Every bounded canonical admissible potential is continuous on the complement of an open set of arbitrarily small $\operatorname {Cap}_1$. The same open set can be chosen for any countable family of such potentials. Proof. Choose smooth admissible $u_ j\downarrow u$. By the preceding lemma these functions converge weakly to $u$ in $H^1$. Mazur's lemma gives finite convex combinations $w_ N$ of terms with $j\geq N$ such that \[  \| w_ N-u\| _{H^1}\leq 8^{-N}.  \] Because $u\leq w_ N\leq u_ N$, they converge pointwise to the canonical function $u$, not just to an unspecified almost-everywhere representative. Put \[  G_{N_0}=\bigcup _{N\geq N_0} \{ |w_{N+1}-w_ N|>2^{-N}\} .  \] The capacity tools imply \[  \operatorname {Cap}_1(G_{N_0}) \leq \sum _{N\geq N_0}4^ N\| w_{N+1}-w_ N\| _{H^1}^2 \leq C\sum _{N\geq N_0}16^{-N}\longrightarrow 0.  \] Outside $G_{N_0}$, the successive differences form a uniformly summable series. Thus $w_ N$ converge uniformly there and their limit $u$ is continuous on that closed set. For a countable family, choose the exceptional open sets with capacities less than $\epsilon 2^{-i}$ and take their union. Countable subadditivity proves the last assertion. $\square$

Proposition 8.10.4 . B40742E0DD08 Suppose $u_ j\downarrow u$ and $v_ j\downarrow v$ are bounded canonical admissible potentials with a common uniform bound. Then \[  v_ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ j\longrightarrow v\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u  \] weakly as currents with signed measure coefficients. The same conclusion holds for $v_ j\mu _{u_ j}	o v\mu _ u$. Proof. Bounded convergence gives $u_ j	o u$ in $L^1$. Their complex Hessians therefore converge in distributions. The preceding coefficient bounds are uniform, so this is weak convergence of each signed coefficient measure against continuous compactly supported tests. The trace measures also converge weakly. Quasicontinuity supplies an open $G$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_1(G)<\epsilon $ on whose complement $v$ and every $v_ j$ are continuous. Dini's theorem on the compact set $X\setminus G$ gives uniform convergence there. Extend $v|_{X\setminus G}$ to a continuous function $F$ on $X$ with the same uniform bound, by Tietze's theorem. title: Theorem 8.10.5
section: 8.10 Sobolev capacity and two Hessian factors
text: Theorem 8.10.5 . 0241EC758621 For two bounded admissible potentials $u,v$, the recursive current $D_2(u,v)=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)$ is symmetric in its arguments. If $u_ j\downarrow u$ and $v_ j\downarrow v$ are bounded admissible sequences with a common uniform bound, then \[  D_2(u_ j,v_ j)\longrightarrow D_2(u,v)  \] in distributions. Their shifted positive currents \[  Q_2(u,v)=\bigl (\omega ^2+\omega \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u +\omega \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v+D_2(u,v)\bigr )\wedge \omega ^{n-m}  \] converge weakly as positive currents. For $m=2$ these are positive Radon measures. For $m>2$, the unwedged $D_2$ also converges weakly as a current with measure coefficients. Proof. For smooth admissible approximations $u_ k\downarrow u$ and $v_ k\downarrow v$, the weighted convergence proposition gives \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ k\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k)\longrightarrow \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u).  \] The smooth current on the left is $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ k\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ k$ and is symmetric. Applying the same argument in the opposite order proves $D_2(u,v)=D_2(v,u)$. For the bounded sequences in the statement, weighted convergence followed by $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ gives the asserted simultaneous distributional limit. The displayed subset expansion is the current of 8.9.6 with $p=2$. Its lower-degree terms converge weakly, so its whole distributional limit is $Q_2(u,v)$. Positivity and the uniform local mass bounds turn this into weak convergence of currents of order zero. When $m>2$, the same conclusion for $D_2$ follows from the uniform coefficient bounds below degree $m$ in 8.9.3 . $\square$

title: Lemma 8.10.6
section: 8.10 Sobolev capacity and two Hessian factors
text: Lemma 8.10.6 . 2A6BE9847309 Let $E$ be a compact subset of a smooth real submanifold of codimension two contained in a coordinate chart. Then $\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)=0$. Proof. It suffices to treat a compact subset of a submanifold chart, since finitely many such subsets cover $E$ and the capacity is subadditive. Choose real coordinates $(s,t)$ there, with $t\in \mathbb R^2$ and the submanifold given by $t=0$. Choose $0\leq \eta \leq 1$ smooth, supported in this chart and equal to one near the compact subset. Put $r=|t|$. For $0<\epsilon <1/2$ define \[  h_\epsilon (r)= \begin{cases}  1,& 0\leq r\leq \epsilon ^2,\\  \displaystyle \frac{\log (\epsilon /r)}{\log (1/\epsilon )}, & \epsilon ^2<r<\epsilon ,\\  0,& r\geq \epsilon . \end{cases}  \] The Sobolev function $f_\epsilon =\eta h_\epsilon $ equals one on an open neighborhood of that subset. On the fixed compact coordinate set the Sobolev norm is equivalent to the Euclidean one. Integration in the two normal variables gives \[  \| f_\epsilon \| _{H^1}^2 \leq C\left(\epsilon ^2+ \int _{\epsilon ^2}^{\epsilon } \frac{\mathrm dr}{r\log (1/\epsilon )^2}\right) =C\left(\epsilon ^2+\frac1{\log (1/\epsilon )}\right) \longrightarrow 0.  \] The derivatives of $\eta $ contribute at most $C\epsilon ^2$. Taking the infimum over open neighborhoods proves the assertion. $\square$

title: Example 8.10.7
section: 8.10 Sobolev capacity and two Hessian factors
text: Example 8.10.7 . AEB4F2397BBF There are bounded continuous $\omega $-plurisubharmonic potentials $u,v$ and a compact Borel set $E$ such that \[  \operatorname {Cap}_1(E)=0,\qquad \int _ E Q_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{m-2}>0.  \] Consequently the first-Hessian capacity estimate does not extend to this positive two-factor measure, even within the continuous $\omega $-plurisubharmonic subclass. Proof. Choose holomorphic coordinates $z_ j=x_ j+\mathrm i y_ j$ and a smooth nonnegative cutoff $\chi $ supported in the chart and equal to one on a smaller coordinate box. Extend \[  u=a\chi |x_1|,\qquad v=a\chi |x_2|  \] by zero outside the chart. These functions are globally continuous and bounded. To check their curvature, replace $|x_ j|$ by $g_\delta (x_ j)=(x_ j^2+\delta ^2)^{1/2}$, with $0<\delta \leq 1$. The Hessian of $\chi g_\delta $ has the nonnegative term $\chi \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_\delta $; all its remaining terms are uniformly bounded forms, since $g_\delta $ and $g_\delta '$ are uniformly bounded on the fixed support. Thus $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi g_\delta )\geq -C\omega $ with $C$ independent of $\delta $. Choosing $a>0$ sufficiently small gives $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(a\chi g_\delta )\geq \omega /2$ for both coordinates. Their decreasing limits $u,v$ are therefore $\omega $-plurisubharmonic and admissible. On the box where $\chi =1$, set $\alpha _ j=\frac{\mathrm i}{4\pi }\mathrm dz_ j\wedge \mathrm d\bar z_ j$. The book's normalization gives \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_\delta (x_ j)=\tfrac 12g_\delta ''(x_ j)\alpha _ j, \qquad g_\delta ''(x_ j) =\frac{\delta ^2}{(x_ j^2+\delta ^2)^{3/2}} \longrightarrow 2\delta _{\{ x_ j=0\} }.  \] The measures $g_\delta ^{\prime \prime }(t)\, \mathrm dt$ have mass two, while their mass outside any fixed neighborhood of zero tends to zero. The two smooth factors depend on distinct real variables, so their product is an approximate identity in $(x_1,x_2)$ and converges to the tensor-product measure. By 8.10.5 , locally \[  D_2(u,v)=a^2\delta _{\{ x_1=0\} }\delta _{\{ x_2=0\} } \alpha _1\wedge \alpha _2.  \] Choose $E$ to be a compact piece of $\{ x_1=x_2=0\} $ inside this box with nonempty relative interior. The preceding lemma gives $\operatorname {Cap}_1(E)=0$. On this box, the positive measure $D_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{n-2}$ has strictly positive mass on $E$, since $\omega $ is strictly positive. The smooth term $\omega ^ n$ and the two single-Hessian terms in the expansion \[  Q_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{m-2} =\omega ^ n+\omega ^{n-1}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v) +D_2(u,v)\wedge \omega ^{n-2}  \] have zero mass on $E$: each single-Hessian term is absolutely continuous in the other normal real variable. Hence the asserted mass is strictly positive. A bound by $C\operatorname {Cap}_1(F)^ b$ for all Borel $F$, with any $b>0$, would contradict this choice of $E$. $\square$

title: 8.11 Local capacities and decreasing products
text:
The codimension-two example shows why Sobolev capacity cannot control a product of Hessians. Local capacities built from smooth Hessian measures give the stronger control needed for the recursive currents. Their quasicontinuity estimate comes from an energy variation in which the derivatives of the background remain present. Work on a coordinate ball $U$ with compact closure in a holomorphic chart, with the restriction of $\omega $. For a smooth function in the local unshifted class of 8.9.8 , put \[  \Lambda _ s(f)=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^ s\wedge \omega ^{n-s},\qquad 0\leq s\leq m,  \] where $\Lambda _0(f)=\omega ^ n$. The local mass and gradient estimates needed for the capacity use ordinary smooth products. Lemma 8.11.1 . 370C4F1C4AF0 Fix $K\Subset U$ and $M<\infty $. For smooth local $m$-subharmonic $f_1,\ldots ,f_ q$ with $|f_ i|\leq M$, $0\leq q\leq m$, their mixed trace has mass at most a constant depending only on $K,U,\omega ,m,M$. If also $f$ is smooth in this class and $|f|\leq M$, then, for $q\leq m-1$, \[  \int _ K\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ q \wedge \omega ^{n-q-1}\leq C.  \] Proof. For one potential and a nonnegative compactly supported cutoff $\chi $, closedness of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f$ gives \[  \int \chi (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^ q\omega ^{n-q} =\int f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^{q-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi \omega ^{n-q}).  \] For $q\geq 1$, the absolute-form estimate 8.2.7 applies at degree $q-1<m$. Nested cutoffs and induction, starting with volume, therefore bound the left side by $C M^ q$; replacing $M$ by $1+M$ includes $M=0$. For mixed factors, positivity of every term in the expansion of $(\sum _ i\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ i)^ q\omega ^{n-q}$ bounds the mixed trace by a fixed multiple of the single trace for $\sum _ i f_ i$. This proves the first assertion, including its degree-zero convention. Replace $f$ by $f+M$, so that $0\leq f\leq 2M$ without changing its gradient or Hessian. The identity \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(f^2)=2f\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f+2\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f  \] also shows that $f^2$ belongs to the local cone. Wedge with the remaining $q$ Hessians and $\omega ^{n-q-1}$. The first term on the right is nonnegative, and the mixed mass estimate applied to $f^2$ and the other potentials bounds the second term. The degree used is $q+1\leq m$. A cutoff equal to one on $K$ gives the stated local estimate. $\square$ Definition 8.11.2 . FA49D2074193 For Borel $E\subset U$ define the smooth capacity \[  c_ s(E)=\sup \left\{ \int _ E \Lambda _ s(a): a\in C^\infty (U),\  -1\leq a\leq 0, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\in \overline{\Gamma _ m(\omega )}ight\} ,  \] for $0\leq s\leq m$. Its outer-open version is \[  c_ s^*(E)=\inf \{ c_ s(G):E\subset G\subset U,\  G	ext{ open}\} .  \] A function on a compact $K\Subset U$ is quasicontinuous for this capacity if, for every $\epsilon >0$, it is continuous on $K\setminus G$ for some open $G\subset U$ with $c_ s(G)<\epsilon $. In particular $c_0(E)=\int _ E\omega ^ n$. Each $c_ s$ is monotone, countably subadditive and continuous under increasing unions. For the last assertion, the supremum over competitors commutes with the increasing supremum over sets. Local smooth mass bounds make it finite on compact subsets. The outer capacity $c_ s^*$ is monotone and countably subadditive and agrees with $c_ s$ on open sets. The capacities control mixed traces for smooth local $m$-subharmonic functions $f_1,\ldots ,f_ q$ with a common bound. Choose a fixed smooth strictly plurisubharmonic $b$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b\geq \omega $ on $U$. For $q\leq s$, choose constants $B$ and $L\geq 1$ so that $(f_1+\cdots +f_ q+b-B)/L$ lies in $[-1,0]$. Both constants depend only on the common bound and the fixed data. Positivity of the smooth binomial expansion gives A08EAEC63C44 8.11.3  egin{equation}  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_1+\cdots +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ q)^ q\omega ^{n-q} \leq C \Lambda _ s igl ((	extstyle \sum _ i f_ i+b-B)/L igr ). \end{equation} For $q=0$ the left side is $\omega ^ n$; the same argument applies. Indeed, replacing any of the $s-q$ factors $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b$ by $\omega $ subtracts a nonnegative mixed trace. Thus every such mixed trace, and every coefficient of a smooth product of $q<m$ Hessians, is dominated on Borel sets by $C c_ s$. The latter assertion follows from the absolute mixed-form estimate. Lemma 8.11.4 . 9AF7CFAD9A0B Let $0\leq q\leq m-1$ and let $S$ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form in $\overline{\Gamma _ m(\omega )}$ pointwise. Put $T=S^ q\omega ^{n-q-2}$. For smooth real $f$ and nonnegative Borel weights $a$, supported on a fixed compact set, \[  \left|\int a\, \mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge Tight| \leq C\left(\int a\, \mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \omega \wedge Tight)^{1/2} \left(\int a\, \omega ^2\wedge Tight)^{1/2}.  \] The corresponding inequality with $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \mathrm d\omega $ holds as well. For a mixed product of $q$ cone forms in place of $S^ q$, it suffices to sum these bounds over the finitely many subset sums of its factors. Proof. For $q\leq m-2$, diagonalize $S$ in an $\omega $-unitary frame. Every diagonal coefficient of $S^ q\omega ^{n-q-2}$ is a positive multiple of $S_{q;ij}(\lambda )$ for two omitted coordinates. This is nonnegative by deleted-coordinate positivity, because $q+2\leq m$. The form is a nonnegative sum of simple positive coordinate forms. For one such simple form, only the remaining complex two-plane contributes to a complementary wedge. The coefficients of $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ are uniformly bounded in unitary frames on the fixed compact set. Its wedge with $\mathrm df$ is consequently bounded by a constant times the gradient norm on that plane. The wedges with $\omega ^2$ and with $\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \omega $ give, up to fixed positive constants, one and the square of that norm. Pointwise Cauchy–Schwarz over the simple summands, followed by integral Cauchy–Schwarz with weight $a$, proves the estimate. Conjugation gives the other estimate. For $q=m-1$, at one point choose an $\omega $-unitary coframe $e_ i$ that diagonalizes $S$. Put $\epsilon _ i=\mathrm i e_ i\wedge  ar e_ i$ and $\Omega =\epsilon _1\cdots \epsilon _ n$, so that $\omega =\sum _ i\epsilon _ i$ and $S=\sum _ i\lambda _ i\epsilon _ i$. Writing $B_{ij}=S_{q;ij}(\lambda )$ and $D_ i=S_{q;i}(\lambda )$, ordinary wedge expansion gives \[  S^ q\omega ^{n-q-2} =q!(n-q-2)!\sum _{i<j}B_{ij} \prod _{k
otin \{ i,j\} }\epsilon _ k.  \] Only the remaining two-plane contributes to its wedge with $\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $. If $\partial f=\sum _ i f_ i e_ i$, its absolute density relative to $\Omega $ is bounded by \[  C\sum _{i<j}(|f_ i|+|f_ j|)|B_{ij}|.  \] The constant bounds the tensor coefficients of $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ in all unitary frames on the fixed compact set. Diagonalization is only pointwise; no derivative of this moving frame is taken. 8.2.8 and finite Cauchy–Schwarz bound this sum by \[  C\sum _ i|f_ i|\sqrt{D_ i}\sum _ j\sqrt{D_ j} \leq C\left(\sum _ i|f_ i|^2D_ iight)^{1/2} \left(\sum _ iD_ iight)^{1/2}.  \] Here $\sum _ iD_ i=(n-q)S_ q(\lambda )$. Moreover \[   egin{aligned}  S^ q\omega ^{n-q}& =q!(n-q)!S_ q(\lambda )\Omega ,\  \mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge S^ q\omega ^{n-q-1} & =\kappa q!(n-q-1)!\sum _ i|f_ i|^2D_ i\, \Omega , \end{aligned}  \] where $\kappa =1/(2\pi )$ by the book's $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ normalization. These two densities are nonnegative. Thus the pointwise torsion density is bounded by a constant times their geometric mean. Multiplication by $a$ and integral Cauchy–Schwarz give the assertion, including the cases where either density vanishes. The other wedge is conjugate up to a fixed sign, which does not affect its absolute value. For $q\geq 1$, use the exact polarization identity \[  q!\, \alpha _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \alpha _ q =\sum _{J\subset \{ 1,\ldots ,q\} } (-1)^{q-|J|}\left(\sum _{i\in J}\alpha _ iight)^ q.  \] Every nonempty subset sum remains in the cone. Applying the single power estimate to each term and taking absolute values proves the mixed assertion. At $q=0$ use the single term $S^0=1$. No Cauchy–Schwarz assertion for an arbitrary weakly positive $(n-2,n-2)$-form is needed. $\square$ Lemma 8.11.5 . 9416072D448F Let $f_ j$ be uniformly bounded smooth local $m$-subharmonic functions with $f_ j\downarrow f$, and fix a smaller concentric ball $V\Subset U$. There are uniformly bounded smooth local functions $v_ j\downarrow v$ which equal $f_ j$ on a neighborhood of $\overline V$ and equal one fixed strictly plurisubharmonic $\psi $ on one fixed boundary collar. Moreover $v=f$ near $\overline V$ and $v=\psi $ on that collar. Proof. Write $U=\{ |z|<R\} $ and $|f_ j|\leq M$. Take $\psi =A(|z|^2-R^2)+b$, with $b>M+2$ and then $A$ so large that $\psi <-M-2$ on a neighborhood of $\overline V$. It exceeds $M+2$ on a fixed sufficiently thin boundary collar. Use the regularized maximum $M_\epsilon $ constructed in 8.2.9 . Choose $0<\epsilon _ j\downarrow 0$ with $\epsilon _ j<1$, and put $v_ j=M_{\epsilon _ j}(f_ j,\psi )$. The lemma preserves the local unshifted cone condition. Its two monotonicities give $v_ j\downarrow \max (f,\psi )=v$, and the fixed gaps give the two asserted regions of exact equality. The bounds \[  \max (f_ j,\psi )\leq v_ j\leq \max (f_ j,\psi )+\epsilon _ j/2  \] give a common bound. In particular all differences $v_ k-v_ j$ have support in one fixed compact subset of $U$. $\square$ Proposition 8.11.6 . 390B1CE08171 For the localized sequence in the preceding lemma and $0\leq s\leq m$, \[  c_ s\{ v_ k-v>\delta \} \longrightarrow 0 \qquad (\delta >0).  \] Consequently a uniformly bounded smooth decreasing local sequence has a quasicontinuous pointwise limit on every compact subset of $U$, for each $c_ s^*$ as well as $c_ s$, $0\leq s\leq m$. Proof. The assertion for $s=0$ follows by bounded convergence for volume. Induct on $s$, assuming it for $s-1$, and put $q=s-1$ and $	heta =\omega ^{n-s}$. For $j\geq k$ let $h=v_ k-v_ j\geq 0$. The support of $h$ lies in one fixed compact set $K_0\Subset U$. Smooth capacity domination and the induction hypothesis give, uniformly over all bounded local smooth mixed potentials, 021C38133493 8.11.7  egin{equation}  \int h\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_1\cdots \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_ q\omega ^{n-q} \longrightarrow 0\quad (k	o \infty ). \end{equation} To see this, split at $h=\delta $. On $\{ h\leq \delta \} $ the mass bound gives $C\delta $. On the remaining set use $h\leq v_ k-v$, the capacity bound and the induction hypothesis. Let $k$ tend to infinity before $\delta \downarrow 0$. For $q=0$ this is the volume estimate. Constants are uniform in $j\geq k$ and all potentials with the fixed common bound. Consider the real smooth energy \[  E_ s(w)=\int _ U w(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ s	heta , \qquad w_ t=v_ j+t h,\quad 0\leq t\leq 1.  \] The energies $E_ s(v_ j)$ are bounded: on the fixed collar the integrand is fixed, and the remaining compact set has a uniform smooth mass bound. The positive shifted currents $Q_ p$ converge weakly for $p\leq m$; $Q_ m$ converges as a positive Radon measure. At degree $m$, the convergence assertion for $D_ m$ is distributional. Proof. E64937A67BD2 On $K\Subset U$, the positive shifted currents $Q_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)$, $1\leq p\leq m$, for globally bounded admissible potentials have trace and coefficient variations bounded on Borel $E\subset K$ by $C c_ m^*(E)$. The constants are uniform when all potentials have a common bound. Proof. First take smooth potentials, put $\sigma _ i=\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i$, and choose the fixed local correction $	au =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}ho \geq 2\omega $. title: Lemma 8.11.1
text: Lemma 8.11.1 . 370C4F1C4AF0 Fix $K\Subset U$ and $M<\infty $. For smooth local $m$-subharmonic $f_1,\ldots ,f_ q$ with $|f_ i|\leq M$, $0\leq q\leq m$, their mixed trace has mass at most a constant depending only on $K,U,\omega ,m,M$. If also $f$ is smooth in this class and $|f|\leq M$, then, for $q\leq m-1$, \[  \int _ K\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ q \wedge \omega ^{n-q-1}\leq C.  \] Proof. For one potential and a nonnegative compactly supported cutoff $\chi $, closedness of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f$ gives \[  \int \chi (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^ q\omega ^{n-q} =\int f(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f)^{q-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\chi \omega ^{n-q}).  \] For $q\geq 1$, the absolute-form estimate 8.2.7 applies at degree $q-1<m$. Nested cutoffs and induction, starting with volume, therefore bound the left side by $C M^ q$; replacing $M$ by $1+M$ includes $M=0$. For mixed factors, positivity of every term in the expansion of $(\sum _ i\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f_ i)^ q\omega ^{n-q}$ bounds the mixed trace by a fixed multiple of the single trace for $\sum _ i f_ i$. This proves the first assertion, including its degree-zero convention. Replace $f$ by $f+M$, so that $0\leq f\leq 2M$ without changing its gradient or Hessian. The identity \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(f^2)=2f\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}f+2\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f  \] also shows that $f^2$ belongs to the local cone. Wedge with the remaining $q$ Hessians and $\omega ^{n-q-1}$. The first term on the right is nonnegative, and the mixed mass estimate applied to $f^2$ and the other potentials bounds the second term. The degree used is $q+1\leq m$. A cutoff equal to one on $K$ gives the stated local estimate. $\square$

title: Definition 8.11.2
text: Definition 8.11.2 . FA49D2074193 For Borel $E\subset U$ define the smooth capacity \[  c_ s(E)=\sup \left\{ \int _ E \Lambda _ s(a): a\in C^\infty (U),\  -1\leq a\leq 0, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a\in \overline{\Gamma _ m(\omega )}\right\} ,  \] for $0\leq s\leq m$. Its outer-open version is \[  c_ s^*(E)=\inf \{ c_ s(G):E\subset G\subset U,\  G\text{ open}\} .  \] A function on a compact $K\Subset U$ is quasicontinuous for this capacity if, for every $\epsilon >0$, it is continuous on $K\setminus G$ for some open $G\subset U$ with $c_ s(G)<\epsilon $.

title: Lemma 8.11.4
text: Lemma 8.11.4 . 9AF7CFAD9A0B Let $0\leq q\leq m-1$ and let $S$ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form in $\overline{\Gamma _ m(\omega )}$ pointwise. Put $T=S^ q\omega ^{n-q-2}$. For smooth real $f$ and nonnegative Borel weights $a$, supported on a fixed compact set, \[  \left|\int a\, \mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge T\right| \leq C\left(\int a\, \mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \omega \wedge T\right)^{1/2} \left(\int a\, \omega ^2\wedge T\right)^{1/2}.  \] The corresponding inequality with $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \mathrm d\omega $ holds as well. For a mixed product of $q$ cone forms in place of $S^ q$, it suffices to sum these bounds over the finitely many subset sums of its factors. Proof. For $q\leq m-2$, diagonalize $S$ in an $\omega $-unitary frame. Every diagonal coefficient of $S^ q\omega ^{n-q-2}$ is a positive multiple of $S_{q;ij}(\lambda )$ for two omitted coordinates. This is nonnegative by deleted-coordinate positivity, because $q+2\leq m$. The form is a nonnegative sum of simple positive coordinate forms. For one such simple form, only the remaining complex two-plane contributes to a complementary wedge. The coefficients of $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ are uniformly bounded in unitary frames on the fixed compact set. Its wedge with $\mathrm df$ is consequently bounded by a constant times the gradient norm on that plane. The wedges with $\omega ^2$ and with $\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge \omega $ give, up to fixed positive constants, one and the square of that norm. Pointwise Cauchy–Schwarz over the simple summands, followed by integral Cauchy–Schwarz with weight $a$, proves the estimate. Conjugation gives the other estimate. For $q=m-1$, at one point choose an $\omega $-unitary coframe $e_ i$ that diagonalizes $S$. Put $\epsilon _ i=\mathrm i e_ i\wedge \bar e_ i$ and $\Omega =\epsilon _1\cdots \epsilon _ n$, so that $\omega =\sum _ i\epsilon _ i$ and $S=\sum _ i\lambda _ i\epsilon _ i$. Writing $B_{ij}=S_{q;ij}(\lambda )$ and $D_ i=S_{q;i}(\lambda )$, ordinary wedge expansion gives \[  S^ q\omega ^{n-q-2} =q!(n-q-2)!\sum _{i<j}B_{ij} \prod _{k\notin \{ i,j\} }\epsilon _ k.  \] Only the remaining two-plane contributes to its wedge with $\mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $. If $\partial f=\sum _ i f_ i e_ i$, its absolute density relative to $\Omega $ is bounded by \[  C\sum _{i<j}(|f_ i|+|f_ j|)|B_{ij}|.  \] The constant bounds the tensor coefficients of $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega $ in all unitary frames on the fixed compact set. Diagonalization is only pointwise; no derivative of this moving frame is taken. 8.2.8 and finite Cauchy–Schwarz bound this sum by \[  C\sum _ i|f_ i|\sqrt{D_ i}\sum _ j\sqrt{D_ j} \leq C\left(\sum _ i|f_ i|^2D_ i\right)^{1/2} \left(\sum _ iD_ i\right)^{1/2}.  \] Here $\sum _ iD_ i=(n-q)S_ q(\lambda )$. Moreover \[  \begin{aligned}  S^ q\omega ^{n-q}& =q!(n-q)!S_ q(\lambda )\Omega ,\\  \mathrm df\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}f\wedge S^ q\omega ^{n-q-1} & =\kappa q!(n-q-1)!\sum _ i|f_ i|^2D_ i\, \Omega , \end{aligned}  \] where $\kappa =1/(2\pi )$ by the book's $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ normalization. These two densities are nonnegative. Thus the pointwise torsion density is bounded by a constant times their geometric mean. Multiplication by $a$ and integral Cauchy–Schwarz give the assertion, including the cases where either density vanishes. The other wedge is conjugate up to a fixed sign, which does not affect its absolute value. For $q\geq 1$, use the exact polarization identity \[  q!\, \alpha _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \alpha _ q =\sum _{J\subset \{ 1,\ldots ,q\} } (-1)^{q-|J|}\left(\sum _{i\in J}\alpha _ i\right)^ q.  \] Every nonempty subset sum remains in the cone. Applying the single power estimate to each term and taking absolute values proves the mixed assertion. At $q=0$ use the single term $S^0=1$. No Cauchy–Schwarz assertion for an arbitrary weakly positive $(n-2,n-2)$-form is needed. $\square$

title: Lemma 8.11.5
text: Lemma 8.11.5 . 9416072D448F Let $f_ j$ be uniformly bounded smooth local $m$-subharmonic functions with $f_ j\downarrow f$, and fix a smaller concentric ball $V\Subset U$. There are uniformly bounded smooth local functions $v_ j\downarrow v$ which equal $f_ j$ on a neighborhood of $\overline V$ and equal one fixed strictly plurisubharmonic $\psi $ on one fixed boundary collar. Moreover $v=f$ near $\overline V$ and $v=\psi $ on that collar. Proof. Write $U=\{ |z|<R\} $ and $|f_ j|\leq M$. Take $\psi =A(|z|^2-R^2)+b$, with $b>M+2$ and then $A$ so large that $\psi <-M-2$ on a neighborhood of $\overline V$. It exceeds $M+2$ on a fixed sufficiently thin boundary collar. Use the regularized maximum $M_\epsilon $ constructed in 8.2.9 . Choose $0<\epsilon _ j\downarrow 0$ with $\epsilon _ j<1$, and put $v_ j=M_{\epsilon _ j}(f_ j,\psi )$. The lemma preserves the local unshifted cone condition. Its two monotonicities give $v_ j\downarrow \max (f,\psi )=v$, and the fixed gaps give the two asserted regions of exact equality. The bounds \[  \max (f_ j,\psi )\leq v_ j\leq \max (f_ j,\psi )+\epsilon _ j/2  \] give a common bound. In particular all differences $v_ k-v_ j$ have support in one fixed compact subset of $U$. $\square$

title: Proposition 8.11.6
text: Proposition 8.11.6 . 390B1CE08171 For the localized sequence in the preceding lemma and $0\leq s\leq m$, \[  c_ s\{ v_ k-v>\delta \} \longrightarrow 0 \qquad (\delta >0).  \] Consequently a uniformly bounded smooth decreasing local sequence has a quasicontinuous pointwise limit on every compact subset of $U$, for each $c_ s^*$ as well as $c_ s$, $0\leq s\leq m$. Proof. The assertion for $s=0$ follows by bounded convergence for volume. Induct on $s$, assuming it for $s-1$, and put $q=s-1$ and $\theta =\omega ^{n-s}$. For $j\geq k$ let $h=v_ k-v_ j\geq 0$. The support of $h$ lies in one fixed compact set $K_0\Subset U$. Smooth capacity domination and the induction hypothesis give, uniformly over all bounded local smooth mixed potentials, 021C38133493 8.11.7 \begin{equation}  \int h\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_1\cdots \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g_ q\omega ^{n-q} \longrightarrow 0\quad (k\to \infty ). \end{equation} To see this, split at $h=\delta $. On $\{ h\leq \delta \} $ the mass bound gives $C\delta $. On the remaining set use $h\leq v_ k-v$, the capacity bound and the induction hypothesis. Let $k$ tend to infinity before $\delta \downarrow 0$. For $q=0$ this is the volume estimate. Constants are uniform in $j\geq k$ and all potentials with the fixed common bound. Consider the real smooth energy \[  E_ s(w)=\int _ U w(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^ s\theta , \qquad w_ t=v_ j+t h,\quad 0\leq t\leq 1.  \] The energies $E_ s(v_ j)$ are bounded: on the fixed collar the integrand is fixed, and the remaining compact set has a uniform smooth mass bound. Since $h$ vanishes near the boundary, integration by parts and closedness of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t$ give the exact identity CA5C66E53CFA 8.11.8 \begin{equation}  \begin{split}  \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}E_ s(w_ t) & =(s+1)\int h(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t)^ s\theta \\ & \quad +s\int h(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t)^ q \bigl (\mathrm dw_ t\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\theta -\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w_ t\wedge \mathrm d\theta +w_ t\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\theta \bigr ). \end{split} \end{equation} Here \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm d\theta & =(n-s)\mathrm d\omega \wedge \omega ^{n-s-1},\\  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\theta & =(n-s)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega \wedge \omega ^{n-s-1}\\ & \quad +(n-s)(n-s-1)\mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \omega ^{n-s-2}, \end{aligned}  \] and the analogous $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ formula holds. A zero scalar coefficient means that its term is absent. The two first-order terms in ( 8.11.8 ) tend uniformly to zero by 8.11.4 , the uniform local gradient bound, and ( 8.11.7 ). The last term has the same property by the absolute-form estimate at degree $q<m$. More explicitly, the first torsion integral is bounded by \[  C\left(\int h\, \mathrm dw_ t\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w_ t \wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t)^ q\omega ^{n-q-1}\right)^{1/2} \left(\int h(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w_ t)^ q\omega ^{n-q}\right)^{1/2}.  \] The first factor is bounded since $h$ has a common bound and 8.11.1 applies; the second tends to zero by ( 8.11.7 ). Conjugation handles the other first-order term. Thus, with $e_ k\downarrow 0$ after taking a tail supremum, \[  E_ s(v_ k)-E_ s(v_ j)=(s+1)\Delta _{kj}+r_{kj}, \quad \Delta _{kj}=\int _0^1\int h\Lambda _ s(w_ t)\, \mathrm dt\geq 0, \quad |r_{kj}|\leq e_ k.  \] It follows that $E_ s(v_ j)\leq E_ s(v_ k)+e_ k$ for $j\geq k$. Taking a subsequence $k$ approaching the liminf shows that the bounded energy sequence converges. Hence $\Delta _{kj}\to 0$ uniformly for $j\geq k$. Positivity of the binomial expansion $\Lambda _ s(w_ t)\geq (1-t)^ s \Lambda _ s(v_ j)$ then gives A133A0104951 8.11.9 \begin{equation}  \int h\Lambda _ s(v_ j)\longrightarrow 0 \quad \text{uniformly for }j\geq k. \end{equation} It remains to replace each Hessian factor by a capacity competitor. For any smooth $-1\leq a\leq 0$ in the local cone, put \[  I_\ell =\int h(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^\ell (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a)^{s-\ell }\theta , \qquad \eta _\ell =(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)^\ell (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a)^{s-\ell -1}, \quad 0\leq \ell <s.  \] First-order Stokes, with every metric derivative retained, gives \[  I_\ell =-\int \mathrm dh\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}a\wedge \eta _\ell \theta +\int h\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}a\wedge \eta _\ell \mathrm d\theta .  \] The second term is $o(1)$ uniformly in $a$ and $j\geq k$. Use finite polarization in 8.11.4 ; each subset sum has a uniform local gradient bound and its lower trace is controlled by ( 8.11.7 ). The form $\eta _\ell \theta $ is positive of bidegree $(n-1,n-1)$: a complementary nonnegative rank-one form completes a polarized product of $s\leq m$ cone forms. Its associated Hermitian gradient pairing is nonnegative, so Cauchy–Schwarz and the uniform gradient bound for $a$ give \[  I_\ell \leq C F_\ell (h)^{1/2}+o(1), \qquad F_\ell (h)=\int \mathrm dh\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}h\wedge \eta _\ell \theta .  \] Another exact first-order Stokes identity gives \[  F_\ell (h)= I_{\ell +1} -\int h\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ k\wedge \eta _\ell \theta +\int h\, \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}h\wedge \eta _\ell \mathrm d\theta \leq I_{\ell +1}+o(1).  \] The dropped term is nonnegative. For the last term the same polarized torsion estimate applies: its first gradient factor is uniformly bounded because $h=v_ k-v_ j$, and its second factor tends to zero by ( 8.11.7 ); here $h^2\leq C h$ and the gradient energy of the difference is at most twice the sum of those of $v_ k$ and $v_ j$ for every positive single-power gradient pairing. Starting with ( 8.11.9 ) at $I_ s$, finite backward induction gives $I_0\to 0$ uniformly in $a$ and $j\geq k$. Chebyshev's inequality now yields $c_ s\{ v_ k-v_ j>\delta \} \leq \delta ^{-1}\sup _ a I_0$. These sets increase to $\{ v_ k-v>\delta \} $ as $j\to \infty $. Continuity of $c_ s$ under increasing unions proves the induction. For any one $0\leq s\leq m$, choose $k_ N$ so that the open sets $G_ N=\{ v_{k_ N}-v>2^{-N}\} $ satisfy $c_ s(G_ N)<\epsilon 2^{-N}$, $N\geq 1$. They are open because $v$ is upper semicontinuous and $v_{k_ N}$ is smooth. On $U\setminus \bigcup _ NG_ N$ these smooth functions converge uniformly to the pointwise limit $v$. Hence $v$ is continuous there. The union has capacity less than $\epsilon $. Boundary localization transfers this conclusion to $f$ on each smaller compact set. Open sets have the same outer capacity, which also proves the assertion for $c_ s^*$. $\square$

title: Theorem 8.11.12
text: Theorem 8.11.12 . C044CD1C65C4 For uniformly bounded admissible potentials $u_ i^ j\downarrow u_ i$ on $X$, the currents $D_ p(u_1^ j,\ldots ,u_ p^ j)$ converge to $D_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)$ in distributions for $p\leq m$, and weakly with measure coefficients for $p<m$. These currents are symmetric in their potentials. For $p<m$ the coefficient convergence also holds after multiplication by a uniformly bounded decreasing admissible weight. The positive shifted currents $Q_ p$ converge weakly for $p\leq m$; $Q_ m$ converges as a positive Radon measure. At degree $m$, the convergence assertion for $D_ m$ is distributional. Proof. Work on a compact coordinate test set. Degree zero is constant. Suppose the result holds for $D_{p-1}$, which has measure coefficients since $p-1<m$. The preceding two lemmas, applied coefficientwise with weight $u_ p^ j$, give convergence of $u_ p^ jD_{p-1}(u_1^ j,\ldots ,u_{p-1}^ j)$. Applying $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ proves distributional convergence at degree $p$. For $p<m$, the uniform coefficient bounds in 8.9.3 upgrade this to weak convergence of measures, by smooth approximation of compactly supported continuous tests. The same weighted lemma gives the additional weighted conclusion. For each fixed list choose simultaneous smooth decreasing global approximations. Their smooth raw Hessian wedges are symmetric. The convergence just proved identifies their limit with $D_ p$ in any ordering, proving symmetry without an exchange of previously unproved iterated limits. The subset expansion for $R_ p$ uses fixed smooth powers of $\omega $, so its distributional convergence and symmetry follow from those of $D_ I$. Its wedge $Q_ p$ is positive with uniform local masses by 8.9.6 . Distributional convergence and these mass bounds imply weak convergence as an order-zero positive current, including the Radon measure conclusion at $p=m$. A partition of unity on a finite coordinate cover proves the global assertions. $\square$

title: Lemma 8.11.13
text: Lemma 8.11.13 . E64937A67BD2 On $K\Subset U$, the positive shifted currents $Q_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)$, $1\leq p\leq m$, for globally bounded admissible potentials have trace and coefficient variations bounded on Borel $E\subset K$ by $C c_ m^*(E)$. The constants are uniform when all potentials have a common bound. Proof. First take smooth potentials, put $\sigma _ i=\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i$, and choose the fixed local correction $\tau =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho \geq 2\omega $. Then $\beta _ i=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ i+\rho )=\sigma _ i+(\tau -\omega )$ lies in the same local cone. Since $\tau -\omega \geq 0$, mixed positivity gives \[  0\leq \int _ E Q_ p\wedge \omega ^{m-p} \leq \int _ E\beta _1\cdots \beta _ p\omega ^{n-p} \leq C c_ m(E),\qquad E\subset K.  \] Here $Q_ p\wedge \omega ^{m-p}=\sigma _1\cdots \sigma _ p\omega ^{n-p}$. The last bound follows from smooth mixed-trace domination at $s=m$ for the bounded corrected potentials and a normalized bounded sum with a fixed strictly plurisubharmonic function. Positivity of $Q_ p$ bounds each of its coefficient variations on the compact coordinate set by a fixed multiple of its trace measure. For bounded potentials choose the smooth decreasing global approximations already established in the chapter. The joint convergence in 8.11.12 identifies their positive-current limit with the previously constructed $Q_ p$. On a compact neighborhood of $K$ inside $U$, lower semicontinuity on open sets preserves trace and coefficient variation estimates. For an arbitrary open $G\supset E$ intersect with a fixed relatively compact neighborhood of $K$ before taking this limit; its capacity is at most $c_ m(G)$. Therefore every such trace or variation measure $\mu $ satisfies $\mu (E)\leq Cc_ m(G)$. Infimize over $G$ to obtain the asserted outer-open bound. The constants of the smooth estimates are independent of the approximation index. The argument does not multiply a rough current of positive order or use an unproved rough diagonal polynomial expansion. $\square$

title: Theorem 8.11.14
text: Theorem 8.11.14 . 945FEE7DBDC5 Suppose $a_ j\downarrow a$ and $u_ i^ j\downarrow u_ i$ are bounded canonical global admissible potentials with common bounds. Then, for $1\leq p\leq m$, \[  a_ j Q_ p(u_1^ j,\ldots ,u_ p^ j) \longrightarrow a Q_ p(u_1,\ldots ,u_ p)  \] weakly as currents with measure coefficients. At $p=m$ this is weak convergence of weighted Radon measures. Proof. Work on a compact coordinate test set. By 8.11.12 , every coefficient measure of the positive shifted currents converges weakly and has a uniform local variation bound. 8.11.13 strengthens this to domination by $C c_ m^*$ on Borel sets. 8.11.10 makes the canonical weights $a_ j$ and $a$ quasicontinuous for this capacity. Apply 8.11.11 with $s=m$ to each coefficient, and then use a finite partition of unity. At $p=m$, $Q_ m$ is a positive Radon measure, so this also gives the stated weighted measure convergence. $\square$

title: 8.12 Locality and maxima of bounded potentials
search_title: Locality and maxima of bounded potentials
section: 8.12 Locality and maxima of bounded potentials
text: Where one bounded admissible potential is strictly larger than another, the maximum has the same positive Hessian current as the larger potential. These strict comparison sets need not be open. Quasicontinuity gives cutoffs whose products with the approximating currents converge, allowing smooth locality to pass to these sets. Proposition 8.12.1 . 9989CBEEE646 Let $u,v$ be bounded admissible, put $w=\max \{ u,v\} $, and fix $1\leq p\leq m$. For any bounded admissible $t_2,\ldots ,t_ p$, \[  \mathbf1_{\{ u>v\} }Q_ p(w,t_2,\ldots ,t_ p) =\mathbf1_{\{ u>v\} }Q_ p(u,t_2,\ldots ,t_ p).  \] The equality is coefficientwise as currents with measure coefficients. The corresponding equality on $\{ v>u\} $ follows by exchanging $u,v$. Proof. Choose smooth uniformly bounded decreasing approximations of all the potentials by 8.6.6 . Construct $w_ j$ by 8.2.9 . Work on one compact coordinate test set. Fix $\delta >0$ and a smooth $\chi _\delta :\mathbb R\to [0,1]$ that vanishes for $s\leq \delta /2$ and equals one for $s\geq \delta $. For $j$ large enough that $\epsilon _ j<\delta /2$, ordinary smooth locality gives \[  \chi _\delta (u_ j-v_ j)Q_ p(w_ j,t_2^ j,\ldots ,t_ p^ j) =\chi _\delta (u_ j-v_ j)Q_ p(u_ j,t_2^ j,\ldots ,t_ p^ j).  \] Indeed, wherever the weight is nonzero, $w_ j=u_ j$ on an open neighborhood. The equality elsewhere follows from its zero weight. Both sequences of positive currents converge by 8.11.12 ; every coefficient variation is uniformly dominated by $C c_ m^*$ by 8.11.13 . The potentials and their limits are quasicontinuous by 8.11.10 . Apply 8.11.11 with $s=m$ and $F(x,y)=\chi _\delta (x-y)$ to the real and imaginary parts of each coefficient. Passing to the limit gives the same identity with $u,v,w,t_2,\ldots ,t_ p$. Choose the cutoffs so that $\chi _\delta (s)\to \mathbf1_{\{ s>0\} }$ pointwise as $\delta \downarrow 0$. Dominated convergence against the fixed finite coefficient variations on the test set gives the asserted restriction. A partition of unity proves it globally. $\square$ On the contact set, a positive constant shift gives a strict comparison before the limit is taken. Decreasing the shift then recovers that set by dominated convergence for a fixed measure. Theorem 8.12.2 . 655B0BBF4F9C Let $u,v$ be bounded admissible. Fix $1\leq r\leq m$ and bounded admissible $z_1,\ldots ,z_{m-r}$. Define the positive Radon measure \[  \mu _ r(t)=Q_ m(\underbrace{t,\ldots ,t}_{r},z_1,\ldots ,z_{m-r}).  \] For $w=\max \{ u,v\} $, \[  \mu _ r(w)\geq \mathbf1_{\{ u\geq v\} }\mu _ r(u) +\mathbf1_{\{ u<v\} }\mu _ r(v).  \] The inequality with $u,v$ exchanged also holds. Proof. Symmetry and 8.12.1 , applied to the $r$ slots, give $\mu _ r(w)=\mu _ r(v)$ on $\{ u<v\} $ and $\mu _ r(w)=\mu _ r(u)$ on $\{ u>v\} $. To include the contact set, put $w_\epsilon =\max \{ u+\epsilon ,v\} $. Strict locality and invariance under addition of constants give \[  \mu _ r(w_\epsilon )\geq \mathbf1_{\{ u+\epsilon >v\} }\mu _ r(u).  \] The invariance follows from the smooth products and their joint decreasing limits. As $\epsilon \downarrow 0$, $w_\epsilon \downarrow w$, so the left side converges weakly to $\mu _ r(w)$. Against any nonnegative continuous compactly supported test function, the right side converges by dominated convergence for the fixed measure $\mu _ r(u)$ to $\mathbf1_{\{ u\geq v\} }\mu _ r(u)$. This proves the measure inequality on the contact set as well as on $\{ u>v\} $. On its disjoint complement $\{ u<v\} $, the already proved equality supplies $\mu _ r(v)$. Restricting the positive measures to these two Borel sets and adding gives the assertion. Exchanging $u,v$ gives its other form. $\square$ Convex rescaling also supplies a positive background term in the measure. Lemma 8.12.3 . 132BB9E1B1F5 For bounded admissible $v$, $0\leq \alpha \leq 1$ and a real constant $b$, the function $v_\alpha =\alpha v+b$ is bounded admissible and \[  H_ m(v_\alpha )\geq \alpha ^ m H_ m(v)+(1-\alpha )^ m\omega ^ n.  \] Proof. Take smooth decreasing uniformly bounded admissible $v_ j\downarrow v$. Cone convexity makes $\alpha v_ j+b$ admissible because \[  \omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\alpha v_ j+b) =\alpha (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ j)+(1-\alpha )\omega .  \] For $\alpha >0$, an upper test $q$ for $\alpha v+b$ gives the upper test $(q-b)/\alpha $ for $v$. The same convex combination of forms therefore proves admissibility of the limit. For $\alpha =0$ the potential is constant. The pointwise decreasing limit has the displayed canonical affine values. Expand the smooth top product. Every mixed term is positive by polarized Gårding positivity. Keeping the two extreme terms gives \[  H_ m(\alpha v_ j+b)\geq \alpha ^ m H_ m(v_ j) +(1-\alpha )^ m\omega ^ n.  \] Joint decreasing convergence from 8.11.12 passes this inequality against each nonnegative continuous test to the asserted inequality of positive Radon measures. $\square$ The weighted limits also pass integration by parts against metric derivatives. A truncation just above the infimum then excludes zero Hessian mass for a bounded potential. Lemma 8.12.4 . 3A8C156268BF Put $k=m-1$ and $\ell =n-m$. For bounded admissible $t_1,\ldots ,t_ k$, let $T=R_ k(t_1,\ldots ,t_ k)\wedge \omega ^\ell $. Then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T$ is a signed Radon measure. If bounded admissible $t_ i^ j\downarrow t_ i$ have a common bound, these measures converge weakly, also after multiplication by any continuous function of finitely many uniformly bounded decreasing admissible potentials. Proof. The subset definition and the torsion formulas in 8.9.7 give, in distributions, \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T={}& \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\omega \wedge \left(\sum _{a=1}^ kR_{k-1}^{\widehat a}\omega ^\ell +\ell R_ k\omega ^{\ell -1}\right)\\ & +2\, \mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \sum _{a<b}R_{k-2}^{\widehat a\widehat b}\omega ^\ell \\ & +2\ell \, \mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge \sum _{a=1}^ kR_{k-1}^{\widehat a}\omega ^{\ell -1}\\ & +\ell (\ell -1)\, \mathrm d\omega \wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}\omega \wedge R_ k\omega ^{\ell -2}. \end{aligned}  \] The sum with two hats is absent when $k=1$, and the last term is absent when $\ell =1$. Every factor $R_ r$ has degree $r\leq k<m$, so its coefficients are signed measures. Expanding each $R_ r$ over subsets expresses the displayed measure as fixed smooth forms wedged with raw currents $D_ p$ of degrees $p\leq m-1$. 8.11.10 therefore bounds its variation locally by $C c_{m-1}^*$, uniformly under common bounds on the potentials. Joint convergence follows from 8.11.12 applied to this expansion. All the canonical weights are quasicontinuous for $c_{m-1}^*$. 8.11.11 , with $s=m-1$, thus proves the weighted assertion coefficientwise on a finite coordinate cover. A partition of unity gives it on $X$. The term involving $R_ k\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\omega ^\ell )$ retains degree $m-1$; the argument requires no coefficient estimate in degree $m$. $\square$ Proposition 8.12.5 . BB9187C844DA Every bounded admissible potential $u$ has \[  \int _ X H_ m(u)>0.  \] No differential identities for powers of $\omega $ are required. Proof. Suppose instead that $H_ m(u)=0$. Fix $s>0$, set $c=\inf _ Xu+s$, and put $w=\max \{ u,c\} $. The upper semicontinuity of $u$ makes $U=\{ u<c\} $ open, and the definition of the infimum makes it nonempty. Moreover $0\leq w-u\leq s$ and this difference is zero outside $U$. The maximum is bounded admissible with its canonical pointwise values by 8.2.9 . For $0\leq q\leq m$, define the positive Radon measures \[  \mu _ q=Q_ m(\underbrace{u,\ldots ,u}_{q}, \underbrace{w,\ldots ,w}_{m-q}).  \] Thus $\mu _ m=H_ m(u)=0$. For $q<m$, let $T_ q$ be the sum of $m-q$ currents with $q+r$ slots equal to $u$ and $m-q-1-r$ slots equal to $w$, for $0\leq r<m-q$, each of degree $m-1$ and wedged with $\omega ^{n-m}$. In smooth notation this is \[  T_ q=\sum _{r=0}^{m-q-1} (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^{q+r} (\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w)^{m-q-1-r}\omega ^{n-m}.  \] Here each displayed product denotes the symmetric shifted current $R_{m-1}$ of ( 8.9.5 ), wedged with $\omega ^{n-m}$. Choose smooth bounded admissible $u_ j\downarrow u$ and the regularized maxima $w_ j=M_{\epsilon _ j}(u_ j,c)\downarrow w$, where $\epsilon _ j\downarrow 0$, as in 8.2.9 . Both lists have a common bound. The smooth polynomial identity and Stokes' theorem on the compact manifold give \[  \int _ X(\mu _ q^ j-\mu _ m^ j) =\int _ X(w_ j-u_ j)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q^ j.  \] Joint decreasing convergence passes the left side to its limit. The preceding lemma, with $F(x,y)=y-x$ and the decreasing lists $u_ j,w_ j$, passes the right side to its limit. Hence \[  \int _ X\mu _ q=\int _ X(w-u)\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q.  \] The difference of the two decreasing sequences need not itself decrease; the continuous two-variable weight is essential here. On the open set $U$, the potential $w$ is constant. Locality of the raw recursion therefore sets every factor $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w$ to zero there, so that its shifted factors become $\omega $. The formula in the preceding lemma expresses $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q|_ U$ as finitely many smooth metric-derivative forms wedged with powers of $\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ of degrees at most $m-1$. Use smooth admissible approximations to $u$ and the constant $c$ in these local expressions; their limits are the same restricted currents. For those smooth approximations, the absolute mixed-form estimate 8.2.7 bounds each such term by a constant times the corresponding positive trace, and therefore by $C\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\mu _ r$ on $U$ after taking joint limits. More explicitly, a term with $r$ factors is bounded by $C(\omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ r\omega ^{n-r}$; this is $C\mu _ r$ on $U$. Against compactly supported nonnegative tests in $U$, weak convergence and lower semicontinuity of total variation preserve the estimate. Exhaustion gives the measure inequality \[  \mathbf1_ U|\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}T_ q| \leq C\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\mathbf1_ U\mu _ r.  \] Here $C$ depends only on $\omega ,m,n$, not on $u$ or $s$; a fixed finite coordinate cover bounds all the smooth metric coefficients. Since $w-u$ vanishes outside $U$, positivity gives \[  \int _ U\mu _ q\leq \int _ X\mu _ q \leq Cs\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\int _ U\mu _ r \qquad (0\leq q<m).  \] Summing these $m$ inequalities and choosing $s>0$ with $mCs<1$ forces $\sum _{r=0}^{m-1}\int _ U\mu _ r=0$. But locality gives $\mu _0=\omega ^ n$ on the nonempty open set $U$, whose volume is positive. This contradiction proves the result. $\square$

text: Theorem 8.12.2 . 655B0BBF4F9C Let $u,v$ be bounded admissible. Fix $1\leq r\leq m$ and bounded admissible $z_1,\ldots ,z_{m-r}$. Define the positive Radon measure \[  \mu _ r(t)=Q_ m(\underbrace{t,\ldots ,t}_{r},z_1,\ldots ,z_{m-r}).  \] For $w=\max \{ u,v\} $, \[  \mu _ r(w)\geq \mathbf1_{\{ u\geq v\} }\mu _ r(u) +\mathbf1_{\{ u<v\} }\mu _ r(v).  \] The inequality with $u,v$ exchanged also holds.
